premise.reason: Stage A2 screens 217 pocket assemblies down to the top-10 that Stage B consumes. Its TIMEOUT tail earns the same exemption as A1's, and the argument is made from what the stage is FOR rather than from TIMEOUT being the same kind of flag. (1) The timeouts are observed outcomes, not censored ones. Re-running the whole stage at a 12.0s cap instead of 4.0s moves cp from 0.51389 to 0.51392 - three ten-thousandths of a percentage point. Tripling the window converts essentially no timeout into a catch, so a ball still moving at 4s is not one that was about to be caught; it is one that is not going to be. (2) The tail does not touch the selection. Across the 217 cfgs the per-cfg timeout rate runs 0.00%-49.06% (sd 17.86%), but in the selected top-10 it is mean 0.08% and max 0.18%. Every assembly A2 actually hands to Stage B would pass the 1% gate on its own; the aggregate exceeds 1% only because of assemblies the stage is in the business of rejecting. A high timeout rate IS the signal of a bad pocket, which is what this stage is built to detect. (3) The alternative denominator is the biased one. Ranking on cp/resolved instead of cp/trials changes 6 of the top 10, and it changes them in the wrong direction: removing non-settling trials from the denominator rewards an assembly for failing to resolve. The negative correlation between timeout rate and cp (-0.476) is the funnel working, not a distortion. (4) Solver validity is clean: IMPACTS_EXHAUSTED is 0.0099% over non-stalled trials after the LAB-23 metric fix, three orders of magnitude under the gate. Measured 14.8952% flagged excluding STALLED, of which TIMEOUT is 14.8854pp. Ceiling set at 17% as a bound with headroom over the measurement, not as a measurement.
